description.value: The first four image volumes of each run were discarded; preprocessing included rigid-body transformation, slice timing, normalization to MNI space, smoothing, high-pass filtering, and prewhitening.

spans.text: Preprocessing included rigid‐body transformation (realignment) and slice timing to correct for head movement and slice acquisition delays. The images were then normalized to MNI space using nonlinear warping implemented in SPM2 using the mean of all functional volumes as a template and then smoothed with a Gaussian filter of 8 mm full‐width at half maximum (FWHM) to increase the signal‐to‐noise ratio and to facilitate group analyses. The time series for each participant was high‐pass filtered at 128 s and prewhitened by means of an autoregressive model AR(1) [Friston et al., 2002].
Imaging data were analyzed using SPM2 (http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm).

description.value: The study tested whether conditional and syllogistic deductive reasoning recruit common or distinct neural processes during premise encoding and integration.

spans.text: Our central aim here was to provide direct evidence of association and/or dissociation of reasoning‐related activations for different types of reasoning problems, specifically conditional and syllogistic problems.

design.value: Within-participants event-related fMRI design comparing conditional and syllogistic deductive problems, with factorial manipulations of task type, problem type, and premise integrability.

spans.text: The deductive problems consisted of two factors-integrability (integrable vs. nonintegrable premises) and type of sentence (syllogistic vs. conditional problems).
